nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiCo-LDH synthesis
nodes.procedure: Cobalt nitrate hexahydrate (1 mmol), nickel nitrate hexahydrate (0.5 mmol), and methenamine were added to methanol (30 mL). Then, a piece of treated carbon cloth was immersed into the aforementioned solution in a 50 mL autoclave, reacted at 180°C for 12 h, and naturally cooled to 25°C. Finally, the film was washed carefully with water and dried overnight at 60°C.

nodes.source_text: Preparation of NiCo-LDH: The typical reaction conditions for the preparation of NiCo-LDH were as follows. Cobalt nitrate hexahydrate (1 mmol), nickel nitrate hexahydrate (0.5 mmol), and methenamine were added to methanol (30 mL).

nodes.name: Hydrothermal sulfuration to NiCo2S4
nodes.procedure: A piece of NiCo-LDH was immersed in the Na2S solution (0.1 M), reacted at 160°C for 8 h, and naturally cooled to 25°C. The successfully prepared NiCo2S4 film was washed with water and dried for 5 h at 60°C.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal ReS2 deposition on NiCo2S4
nodes.procedure: In a typical procedure, the as-prepared NiCo2S4 samples were immersed in the solution of deionized water (25 mL) and absolute ethanol (5 mL) containing ammonium perrhenate (50 mg), thiourea (80 mg), and NH4F. The autoclave was maintained at 220°C for 6 h. After cooling, the samples were washed 3 times with ethanol and deionized water and dried overnight in a vacuum oven at 60°C.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show NiCo₂S₄/ReS₂ forms hierarchical nanosheet arrays with ReS₂ nanosheets (several nm thick) decorated on NiCo₂S₄ surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The nanosheet arrays of ReS₂ were observed after the deposition process onto the NiCo₂S₄ surface with the thickness of several nanometers (Figure 1d), establishing a hierarchical structure of NiCo₂S₄ nanosheets decorated with 2D ReS₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms formation of NiCo₂S₄/ReS₂ 2D-2D nanocomposites with wrinkled morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscope (TEM) images of NiCo₂S₄/ReS₂ correspond well with the scanning electron microscope (SEM) images (Figure 1d,e; Figure S1c, Supporting Information), revealing adequate formation of the NiCo₂S₄/ReS₂ 2D-2D nanocomposites.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM shows lattice fringes of 0.78 nm for ReS₂ (001) plane and 0.28 nm for NiCo₂S₄ (311) plane; ReS₂ d-spacing extended compared to pristine ReS₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The visible lattice fringe with interplanar spacings of 0.78 nm correlates with the d-spacings of the (001) plane of ReS₂ (Figure 1g) and 0.28 nm corresponds to the d-spacings of the (311) plane of NiCo₂S₄ (Figure 1h).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping shows uniform dispersion of Ni, Co, Re, and S; line scan reveals wider Re distribution indicating ReS₂ decoration over NiCo₂S₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1i, the elemental mapping analysis revealed that Ni, Co, Re, and S were uniformly dispersed on the NiCo₂S₄/ReS₂ nanosheet.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows NiCo₂S₄ peaks at 31.7°, 38.4°, 50.6°, 55.4° (311,400,333,440 planes); ReS₂ (002) peak splits to 9.2° and 17.0° indicating extended interlayer distance.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The characteristic peaks at 2θ = 31.7°, 38.4°, 50.6°, and 55.4° were assigned to the (311), (400), (333), and (440) planes of NiCo₂S₄ (JCPDS 20-0782), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows NiCo₂S₄ peaks at 373.9, 669.3 cm⁻¹ and ReS₂ peaks at 155.7, 201.6, 309.8 cm⁻¹ (E_g, A_g, E_g-like); no shifts after hybridization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The typical stretching vibration peaks of NiCo₂S₄ centered at 373.9 and 669.3 cm⁻¹ were found for pristine NiCo₂S₄. In addition, three main peaks located at 155.7, 201.6, and 309.8 cm⁻¹, which can be assigned to the in-plane (E_g) vibration, out-of-plane (A_g) vibration, and in-plane (E_g-like) vibration of ReS₂, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows S 2p shift indicating Ni-S-Re/Co-S-Re bonds; Re 4f shifts to lower energy; Co 2p and Ni 2p shift to higher energy with increased Co³⁺/Co²⁺ ratio (1.7) and high-spin states evidenced by satellites and Δ_Ni values.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution X-ray photoelectron spectra (XPS) were employed to investigate the interfacial electronic interactions of NiCo₂S₄/ReS₂ (Figure 2c-f; Figure S6, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: SQUID shows μ_eff of NiCo₂S₄/ReS₂ (0.633 μ_B) higher than NiCo₂S₄ (0.439 μ_B), confirming spin-crossover to higher spin state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We confirmed that the μ_eff of NiCo₂S₄/ReS₂ (0.633 μ_B) is higher than that of NiCo₂S₄ (0.439 μ_B), providing evidence for the higher spin state of the NiCo₂S₄/ReS₂ than NiCo₂S₄.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows charge transfer resistance R_ct of 16.25 Ω for NiCo₂S₄/ReS₂ at 85 mV overpotential in alkaline HER (lowest among samples).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lowest R_ct value of 16.25Ω was observed for NiCo₂S₄/ReS₂, which was far smaller than those of the other samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in non-Faradaic region gives double-layer capacitance C_dl of 93.20 mF cm⁻² for NiCo₂S₄/ReS₂, indicating largest ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In particular, the C_dl of NiCo₂S₄/ReS₂ (93.20 mF cm⁻²) is much higher than those of NiCo₂S₄ and ReS₂ (Figure 3d), indicating the largest ECSA of NiCo₂S₄/ReS₂ in the HER for abundant active sites.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows R_ct of 18.94 Ω for NiCo₂S₄/ReS₂ at 126 mV overpotential in acidic HER (lowest among samples).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, it has the smallest R_ct (18.94Ω) among all the prepared samples (Figure 4c), confirming the faster charge transfer rate of the HER.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV gives largest C_dl and ECSA for NiCo₂S₄/ReS₂ in acidic HER among tested catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The largest C_dl and ECSA values were also observed for NiCo₂S₄/ReS₂, which is beneficial for providing abundant active sites and facilitating mass/ion diffusion (Figure 4d; Figure S13, Supporting Information).
